messages.author: c88e28774bbd855d
messages.subject: Simulating standardized data - bug?
parts:
Dear all,

I am trying to get standardized data from a simulation model. Here is my code:

d <- simulateData("y ~ .5*x + .2*z \n x ~~ .5*z",

  standardized=TRUE,sample.nobs=100000)


I thought that "standardized=TRUE" would generate a model where the implied variances should all be 1. But this doesn't seem to be the case here:


var( d$y )

[1] 1.289459


The specified parameters are "legal" as in there exists a model with these coefficients, variances all 1, and positive definite covariance matrix. So my feeling is that it should be possible to get standardized results.


Am I misunderstanding something here? I am using the latest lavaan version.


Best regards

Johannes


PS while trying to investigate the issue I saw this line in the "simulateData" source code:


if (any(lav$ustart[lambda.idx] >= 1)) {

    warning("lavaan WARNING: standardized=TRUE but factor loadings are >= 1.0")

}


Should this perhaps be


if (any(abs(lav$ustart[lambda.idx]) >= 1)) {

    warning("lavaan WARNING: standardized=TRUE but factor loadings are >= 1.0")

}


?

messages.author: c88e28774bbd855d
messages.subject: Re: Simulating standardized data - bug?
parts:
Hi all,

here's a more complete example to clarify my problem.

Take the following model

m <- lavaanify("
y ~ (1.2) * x + (-1) * z
x ~~ .8*z
y ~~ .48*y
z ~~ 1*z
x ~~ 1*x
",fixed.x=FALSE)

This model already implies a standardized covariance matrix as you can check:

cov(simulateData(m,sample.nobs=100000))


But if you do the following: 


cov(simulateData(m,sample.nobs=100000,standardized=TRUE))


Then


- you get a warning that the standardized regression coefficient y~x is > 1.0. I don't know what should be wrong with that -- these are not correlations, so as long as the implied covariance matrix is still positive definite (which it is) it should be fine?


- the function overrides the specified residual variances (politely giving a warning) and replaces them by other values that no longer imply a standardized covariance matrix.


Any help how to interpret this behaviour would be very much appreciated.


Best regards

Johannes

messages.author: c1cccdf0b808f922
messages.subject: Re: Simulating standardized data - bug?
parts:
Hi all,
Johannes is right - the simulateData() command throws an error if standardized regression coefficients larger than 1 are encountered, but that must be an error. 
Standardized regression coefficients in MULTIPLE (but not single) regression are only bounded by the specific constellation of inter-correlations of variables, but are not strictly bounded by |1|.
Here is another counter-example (done outside lavaan):

library(MASS)
Sigma <- matrix(c(1,.95,.60,
                  .95,1,.80,
                  .80,.60,1),3,3)
d1 <- data.frame(mvrnorm(n = 1000, rep(0, 3), Sigma, empirical = TRUE))
names(d1) <- c("x1","x2","y")
var(d1) #variables are indeed standardized with mean 0 and total variance 1
lm(y~x1+x2,data=d1) #regression model with large coefficient values >1


The covariance matrix used for data-generation is standardized (mean 0, var 1), and the regression coefficients are all substantially larger than 1. 

This also happens if all coefficients are negative:

cov(simulateData("y ~ .5*x + .2*z \n x ~~ .5*z",
                  standardized=TRUE,sample.nobs=100000))


This model above also implies a positive-definite correlation matrix, in which the predictors are correlated -.7, and the two correlations between predictors and outcome is -.36 each. 

I looked at the R code for simulateData but can't figure out quite yet where the error lies. 
Felix

messages.author: c88e28774bbd855d
messages.subject: Re: Simulating standardized data - bug?
parts:
Dear all

@Felix thanks for your help. It's good to see that indeed there's nothing wrong with standardized coefficients > 1.

After digging more into this issue, I now do believe that this is a bug. The simulateData function currently attempts to standardize as follows:

- set exogenous variables to variance 1 and all residual variances to 0
- compute implied covariance matrix Sigma.hat
- set residual i to 1 - Sigma.hat[i,i]

While this does work in some cases (e.g. simple factor models), in general I believe this is not correct. Below is a derivation of how to standardize for DAG models, which is a special case but even in this case the above procedure won't work in general.

Define Beta as the matrix of standardized regression coefficients (i.e. Beta[y,z] = c for y ~ c*z); this is the same as lavaan's Beta matrix.

Then define Lambda = (I-t(Beta))^{-1}, where I is the identity matrix. Then the implied covariance matrix is

Sigma = t(Lambda) * Phi * Lambda

where Phi are the residual variances that we are looking for. Specifically, we wish to find Phi such that

diag( t(Lambda) * Phi * Lambda ) = 1

(where 1 is a vector of all ones)

diag( t(Lambda) * Phi * Lambda ) can be written as t(Lambda)^2 * v, where v = diag(Phi).

In other words, we wish to solve the equation system

t(Lambda)^2 v = 1

Plugging back in the definition of Lambda, the solution is given by

v = (t(I - Beta))^{-2}

So we need to solve a nontrivial linear equation system to find the residual variances. Also, note that this does not require any distinction between exogenous and non-exogenous covariates.

Below is code that implements this procedure, and demonstrates it on one example. Unfortunately I don't know enough about the various classes of models supported by lavaan to fix the simulateData code itself.

Best regards
Johannes



# example model where simulateData( lav, standardized=TRUE ) fails
lav <- lavaanify( "
y ~ (-.5) * x + (.25) * z
x ~ .5*U
z ~ .5*U
")

# use the equation solving approach explained above
ov.names <- vnames(lav, "ov")
Beta <- t(lavaan(lav)@Model@GLIST$beta)

vars <- solve( t(diag(nrow(Beta))-Beta)^2 ) %*% rep(1,nrow(Li))
# or use MASS::ginv instead of solve for near-singularity robustness

var.group <- which(lav$op == "~~" & lav$lhs %in% ov.names & 
        lav$rhs == lav$lhs)

lav$ustart[var.group] <- vars

# check implied covariance matrix

cov(simulateData(lav,sample.nobs=1000000))

On 01/13/2016 11:14 AM, Johannes Textor wrote:
> @Felix thanks for your help. It's good to see that indeed there's
> nothing wrong with standardized coefficients > 1.
Sure, the warning needs to go.
> After digging more into this issue, I now do believe that this is a bug.

After reading the documentation again, I agree. The documentation seems
to suggest that a fully standardized solution will be returned, but the
code was/is less ambitious.

The 'standardized = TRUE' option (which was mainly there with factor
models in mind!) was only meant for those that did not specify the
residual variances (of observed indicators) manually.

The simulateData() function is an old piece of code that I once wrote in
few hours to quickly get some fake data. A serious revision is in order.

@Johannes: would you be so kind to open an issue at lavaan's github page
about this?

Yves.

messages.author: c88e28774bbd855d
messages.subject: Re: Simulating standardized data - bug?
parts:
Hi Yves,

Thanks for your reply. Yes indeed, for factor models where you just want to fill in the residuals of the observed variables, the simple approach should work. I only discovered this because I was calling out to simulateData from an R package that I am writing, where I wanted to simulate data from DAGs with randomly chosen standardized path coefficients.

I now implemented this myself using the algebra outlined above, and tested it on DAGs with up to 50-150 variables. It works well so maybe you can leverage this to simulateData. I'd be happy to help if I can. For now, I'll open an issue on github.

Thanks and best regards
Johannes
